newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion up on lower inflows, seasonal buys.
newsitem.headline: India bullion up on lower inflows, seasonal buys.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closed 40 rupees higher at 7,425 rupees per kg after opening 15 rupees lower at 7,370 rupees against the previous close of 7,385 rupees. Prices bounced back after early losses amid shortage of ready stock.

** Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees higher at 4,800 rupees per 10 grammes after opening 10 rupees higher at 4,790 rupees against the previous close of 4,780 rupees on the back of thin supplies and seasonal buying.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 200 rupees higher at 56,100 rupees per piece after opening at the steady level of 55,900 rupees against the previous close.
Silver (.999) prices closed 40 rupees higher at 7,425 rupees per kg on the back of lower than expected arrivals of imports, coupled with a shortage of ready stock, dealers said.
Prices opened 150 rupees lower at 7,370 rupees per kg in slow physical buying but prices bounced back later in thin arrivals as well as an uptrend in the world market.
Silver was down 60 rupees per kg on Monday but was up 355 rupees per kg last week.
Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees higher at 4,800 rupees per 10 grammes on continued seasonal buying during the day coupled with restricted inflow.
Prices opened 10 rupees higher at 4,790 rupees and lifted further on the back of physical as well as speculative support following recovery in the world market, dealers said.

Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 200 rupees higher at 56,100 rupees per piece against previous closing of 55,900 rupees. They were steady on Monday but were down by 300 rupees per piece during last week.
Overall sentiment was firm at the close amid limited arrivals and speculative enquiries on the back of rally in the world market. (Conversion $1=35.89 rupees)-- Bombay newsroom +91-22 265 9000
